notes: Grade each answer against must / must_not. A case passes only if every must is present and no must_not appears.

cases.prompt: I've built a Claude skill for my FileMaker work. It's a folder with SKILL.md and some reference files, built from a client solution I support. I've never used GitHub. How do I put it on GitHub so other FileMaker developers can use it?
must: Reviews the content for client material before publishing: client or company names, hostnames/server addresses, account names or passwords in script examples, real records or sample data
Puts SKILL.md at the repository root (repo root = skill folder)
Adds a licence and a README that tells people how to install it
Authenticates through the browser (gh auth login or Git Credential Manager), not by typing a GitHub password
Creates a release with a downloadable .zip of the skill folder for Claude.ai / Claude app upload
must_not: Tells the developer to type their GitHub account password at a terminal prompt
Ticks 'Add a README' on github.com/new and then pushes an existing folder without addressing the resulting conflict

cases.prompt: My FileMaker skill is in a public GitHub repo. What do I need to add so Claude Code users can install it with a command, and what command do they run?
must: Adds .claude-plugin/plugin.json to the repo
Adds .claude-plugin/marketplace.json so the repo is its own marketplace (or lists it in an existing marketplace)
Install is two commands: claude plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo> then claude plugin install <name>@<marketplace-name>
The name after @ is the marketplace's name from marketplace.json, not the repo name
must_not: Invents a command such as 'claude skill install' or 'claude skills add <url>'
Says users must clone into ~/.claude/skills as the only option

cases.prompt: Someone tried my FileMaker skill: they clicked Code > Download ZIP on my GitHub repo and uploaded it to Claude in Customize > Skills, and it didn't work. What's wrong?
must: GitHub's source zip wraps everything in a <repo>-main folder and carries every repo file, including .claude-plugin/ and evals
An archive carrying a plugin manifest (.claude-plugin/) is rejected by, or routed away from, the Claude app's skill upload
Fix: attach a purpose-built zip (skill folder with SKILL.md inside, no .claude-plugin, no .git) to a GitHub release and link to that asset from the README
Optionally a .gitattributes export-ignore so GitHub's source zips leave out .claude-plugin/ and evals/
must_not: Says the user just needs to rename the zip or re-upload the same file

cases.prompt: I've fixed some things in my FileMaker skill that's already on GitHub. How do I ship it as version 1.1.0 properly?
must: Bumps the version in every place it lives, kept identical: SKILL.md metadata.version, VERSION file (if used), plugin.json, CHANGELOG heading
Commits, tags v1.1.0 and pushes the tag
Creates a GitHub release (gh release create or the website) with notes from the CHANGELOG
Builds the upload zip from a clean checkout of the tag, not the working folder, and attaches it
Explains plugin users get it via claude plugin marketplace update / plugin update, and zip users must re-download
must_not: Re-uses or moves an already-published tag

cases.prompt: Before making my FileMaker skill repo public I noticed an early commit had a script example with our FileMaker Server admin password in it. I removed it in a later commit. Is it safe to make the repo public now?
must: No: the password is still in the earlier commit in history
Change (rotate) the password first, regardless of anything else
Either rewrite history (git filter-repo or BFG) and force-push, or start a fresh repository from the cleaned files
Re-check history (e.g. git log -p / grep the history) before switching visibility
must_not: Says deleting it in a later commit is enough
Treats rewriting history as making the old password safe without rotating it

cases.prompt: My skill folder for FileMaker has SKILL.md, references, a copy of the client's .fmp12 I used for testing, a SaXML export, and a .env with my Claude API key. What should go on GitHub?
must: The .fmp12 stays out (client data, and binary)
The SaXML export stays out unless scrubbed: it carries client schema, account names and can carry data
The .env stays out; add a .gitignore before the first commit; if the key was ever committed, revoke it
Run git status (or a dry run) and check the staged file list before the first commit
must_not: Suggests committing the .env and making the repo private as sufficient protection

cases.prompt: /cadenceux-github  (Claude Code session in ~/skills/invoice-helper. If you looked, you would find: SKILL.md present with name: invoice-helper; `git status` says 'not a git repository'; `gh auth status` says logged in to github.com as jdoe.)
must: Reports the state found: a skill folder named invoice-helper, no Git repo yet, gh signed in
Routes to first publish and treats tools and sign-in as done
Names scrubbing client material as the next step
Asks before starting; doesn't create a repo or push
must_not: Starts with the full step 1 install instructions as if nothing were set up
Creates a GitHub repo, commits or pushes without asking

must: Asks one question: first publish, shipping an update, or fixing a problem
must_not: Lays out all eight first-publish steps in full before knowing what the developer wants

cases.prompt: I'd like to share my FileMaker skill but I've never had a GitHub account. Where do I start?
must: The developer signs up themselves at github.com (free plan is enough)
Username choice matters: it appears in repo URLs and the install command
Turn on two-factor authentication and keep the recovery codes safe
Keep the email private and use the noreply address for commits
Then sign in with gh auth login through the browser
must_not: Asks the developer for their password or offers to create the account for them
Tells them to type a GitHub password at a terminal prompt

cases.prompt: Are my published skills up to date? (Simulated: review_published_skill.sh ran on ~/skills/invoice-helper and ~/skills/naming-conventions. invoice-helper: versions all 1.2.0, last tag v1.2.0, 3 commits since, GitHub release v1.2.0, open issues 1, installed in Claude Code 1.2.0; ACTION lines: '3 commit(s) since v1.2.0 not released: ship an update', '1 open issue(s) to read'. naming-conventions: versions all 1.1.0, last tag v1.1.0, 0 commits since, GitHub release v1.1.0, installed in Claude Code 1.0.0; ACTION: 'installed copy is 1.0.0, release is 1.1.0: claude plugin marketplace update, then claude plugin update'.)
must: invoice-helper has unreleased changes: route to shipping an update (a new version, not re-using v1.2.0)
Read the open issue before releasing, since a fix could join the same update
naming-conventions: the installed copy is behind; update with claude plugin marketplace update then claude plugin update
Says content freshness (vendor changes, evals) is an audit for cadenceux-skill-creator
Asks before tagging, pushing or releasing
must_not: Tags, pushes or releases without asking
Says everything is up to date
